title: EIP-8298: SETCODEFROM Code Reuse Instruction
description: Adds an instruction that sets an account's code hash from an existing deployed contract.
author: Liyi Guo (@colinlyguo), Ben Adams (@benaadams), Carlos Perez (@CPerezz), Nicolas Consigny (@nconsigny)
laymanDescription: Deploying many contracts that share identical code means paying to store those same bytes over and over. This proposal adds an instruction letting an account set up its own storage and then adopt the code already deployed at another address. It also gives an account a way to permanently retire its original key.
benefits: Factories deploy many instances without paying code deposit gas for identical code
Offers a migration path that permanently disables an account's ECDSA transaction authority
Copies from a live account, so the adopted code is confirmed by current consensus state
tradeoffs: Code exposing the instruction can permanently change account behavior if left unguarded
Delegated code may rewrite the calling account's code, unlike the stricter EIP-6913
ecRecover still recovers a migrated account, so permit-style approvals need EIP-8151
